title: Quantum Topology and Quantum Machine Learning Integration
abstract: Quantum topology, a fundamentally new field of mathematics, offers unique properties that can be leveraged to enhance machine learning algorithms. This paper explores the integration of quantum topology with machine learning, proposing a novel framework to achieve more powerful data analysis and model prediction. We outline the core claims, mechanism, and significance of this integration, emphasizing the potential for breakthroughs across diverse applications, particularly in areas demanding high-dimensional data and complex pattern recognition. The framework proposes a synergistic relationship between the inherent structural properties of quantum topology and the predictive capabilities of machine learning, ultimately aiming to push the boundaries of data-driven discovery.

title: Structured Quantum Stealth Computing Theory
abstract: Quantum Stealth Computing Theory explores the design of structured quantum computing systems, aiming to enhance security and efficiency through a novel approach to key distribution. This paper presents a theoretical framework centered around the manipulation of quantum entanglement to construct a 'structured' quantum computing paradigm. The core mechanism involves analyzing the inherent structure of the quantum computation to identify vulnerabilities and subsequently design a new, enhanced key distribution protocol. The resulting theory proposes a shift in how quantum keys are generated and distributed, offering a potential pathway toward more robust and scalable quantum technologies.

title: Adaptive Topology Learning for Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the concept of adaptive topology learning within neural networks, addressing the limitations of static topological neural networks. The core claim proposes that neural networks can actively learn their topology to adapt to evolving data and task requirements, ultimately leading to more efficient parallel computation. This is achieved through an internal topology learning module that dynamically adjusts network connections and node quantities based on performance metrics. The novelty lies in introducing this self-optimization capability, moving beyond the traditional static nature of topological neural networks. The paper details the theoretical framework, including the mathematical formulation of the topology learning process and the evaluation criteria. We present a methodology for continuous adaptation, emphasizing the role of feedback loops and optimization algorithms. The proposed approach aims to create neural networks that are not only powerful but also inherently adaptable and optimized for specific tasks. The key contributions include a novel framework for adaptive topology learning and a mathematical model to guide this process. ---

title: Module-Based Information Theory Assessment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to information theory assessment utilizing a modular information theory (MINT) framework. The core claim is that MINT allows for dynamic adjustment of algorithm complexity based on input data characteristics, thereby improving algorithm efficiency. The framework decomposes the algorithm's complexity into distinct modules, which are adjusted automatically to optimally model the data's inherent complexity. This dynamic adaptation significantly enhances the ability of MINT to analyze complex data structures. We present a practical implementation demonstrating the framework's effectiveness in several benchmark datasets. The paper details the MINT framework's architecture, the complexity decomposition process, and its impact on performance across various data types. Finally, we discuss the limitations and potential future directions of this approach.

title: Self-Supervised Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding and Temporal Regularization
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has achieved remarkable progress in recent years, particularly with contrastive predictive coding (CPC). However, CPC's performance often degrades when dealing with long-range dependencies within sequential data. This work addresses this limitation by augmenting CPC with a novel temporal regularization term. This regularization penalizes prediction errors not just based on the difference between the predicted and actual future states, but also based on the model's own predicted future states. This encourages temporal coherence and improves the model's ability to capture and utilize long-range dependencies. We demonstrate that this combined approach leads to significant improvements in learning performance compared to standard CPC, particularly in tasks requiring understanding of temporal sequences. The core claim of this work is that Contrastive predictive coding (CPC) can struggle with long-range dependencies in sequential data. The core mechanism is to augment CPC with a temporal regularization term that penalizes prediction errors based on the model's own predicted future states, enforcing temporal coherence. The novelty lies in the combination of CPC with this specific temporal regularization strategy. ---

title: Old Search Trees, New Fruits: A Comparative Analysis Review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of planning and search algorithms as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence via Causal Inference Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) centered around causal inference. The core claim is to construct a system capable of not only explaining the decision-making process of AI models but also performing causal inference on those decisions. The proposed mechanism involves decomposing the model's decision process into a sequence of causal steps, utilizing causal graphs for modeling, and employing counterfactual reasoning for interpretation. Unlike existing XAI methods primarily focused on internal model explanations, this framework addresses the critical need for analyzing the causal relationships underlying AI decisions, offering a more robust and trustworthy approach to understanding and validating AI systems. The framework aims to provide insights into *why* a model made a specific decision, going beyond simply identifying which features contributed to the output. This work lays the groundwork for building AI systems that are not just accurate, but also transparent and accountable.

title: 自适应量子拓扑的量子信息存储与检索
abstract: Quantum information storage and retrieval represents a significant challenge in the field of quantum information science. Traditional approaches often rely on static quantum states, limiting the system's versatility. This paper explores the potential of utilizing self-adaptive quantum topology to design a novel quantum information storage and retrieval framework. We present a conceptual model demonstrating the dynamic adjustment of quantum states based on topological properties, offering a pathway towards more flexible and adaptable quantum data storage and retrieval. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging the inherent adaptability of quantum topology to enable instantaneous and robust quantum state manipulation. This research investigates the implications of this approach, emphasizing its potential to surpass the limitations of conventional methods.

title: Quantum State Dynamics Optimization
abstract: Quantum state dynamics optimization is a rapidly evolving field within quantum computing, aiming to enhance the performance of quantum algorithms through intelligent parameter adjustment. This paper presents a novel algorithm, Quantum State Dynamics Optimization (QSDO), that leverages the concept of dynamic topology to automatically optimize quantum state parameters. We introduce a method that iteratively adjusts the quantum state to minimize errors and maximize fidelity, addressing a key limitation of traditional parameter tuning methods. The core mechanism centers around constructing and manipulating a dynamic topology, allowing for continuous, adaptive parameter adjustments. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, demonstrates its effectiveness through simulations, and discusses its potential impact on quantum computation.

title: Graph-Based Quantum Computation Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computation algorithm based on graph theory, aiming to simplify quantum computations by leveraging graph structure characteristics. Traditional quantum computing often struggles with efficiently utilizing graph structures, leading to complex algorithms. Our approach transforms the core quantum computation process into a graph representation, employing graph nodes and edges to design an optimized quantum computation. The core mechanism focuses on reducing computational complexity through the intelligent design of the graph structure itself. This paper details the algorithm's architecture, the rationale behind the graph representation, and the resulting efficiency gains compared to traditional methods. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this algorithm in solving a specific benchmark problem, highlighting its potential for advancing quantum computing.

title: 基于多智能体协作的概率推理网络
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for probabilistic inference leveraging the power of multi-agent collaboration. The core idea is to distribute the inference task across a network of intelligent agents, each specializing in a particular subset of probabilistic information. Through a carefully designed collaboration mechanism, these agents collectively deduce and update global probability distributions. Furthermore, machine learning algorithms are employed to optimize the collaborative strategies, enhancing both the efficiency and accuracy of the inference process. Unlike traditional centralized approaches, this decentralized architecture offers scalability and robustness, particularly in scenarios involving large and complex datasets. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline key design considerations for implementing such a system. The primary contribution lies in the integration of multi-agent systems with probabilistic inference, leading to improved performance and adaptability.

title: Non-Symmetric Quantum Circuits: A Proof of Universal Computation and Architectural Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum computation centered around non-symmetric quantum circuits. We provide a rigorous mathematical proof demonstrating the universal computational capabilities of these circuits under specific conditions. Furthermore, we propose a dedicated hardware architecture designed for efficient computation using non-symmetric quantum lines. This work challenges the traditional paradigm of symmetric quantum circuits and offers a new perspective on utilizing non-symmetric circuits for quantum computation. Our analysis leverages concepts such as quantum entanglement and decoherence, and highlights the potential for achieving enhanced computational performance through careful circuit design. The key contribution lies in establishing a framework for understanding and exploiting the unique properties of non-symmetric quantum circuits, paving the way for the development of more efficient and versatile quantum computing systems.

title: Solar Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting: A Review of Artificial Intelligence Approaches
abstract: The rapid global expansion of solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity has increased the operational need for accurate generation forecasting to support grid balancing, dispatch, and market participation. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods now dominate this research area, but the resulting literature is large and methodologically fragmented, making it difficult to establish which methods are used, what data they require, and where the principal gaps lie. This paper combines a bibliometric analysis of 3111 records retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (2010–2026) with a technical synthesis of 27 highly cited studies published from 2022 onward, combining the most highly cited works with targeted additions from 2024–2025 covering specific methodological gaps. The bibliometric analysis shows exponential growth in annual output, from three publications in 2010 to 609 in 2025, with keyword evolution tracing a clear methodological trajectory from classical and fuzzy-logic approaches, through shallow and deep neural networks, to transformer- and attention-based architectures since 2023. The technical synthesis finds that classical machine learning remains competitive for day-ahead forecasting with well-structured numerical weather prediction inputs, that convolutional neural network–long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) hybrids dominate the deep-learning literature, and that graph-based and transformer architectures address multi-site and multi-horizon forecasting, respectively. A comparison of reported results shows that absolute error metrics are not directly comparable across studies due to heterogeneous datasets, metrics, temporal resolutions, and climates, although relative improvements within controlled comparisons are directionally consistent. Seven research gaps are identified, including the absence of standardized benchmarks, limited public dataset availability, weak cross-region generalization, and underdeveloped uncertainty quantification.

title: Detect Then Rewrite: A Two-Stage Pipeline for Arabic Toxicity Moderation under Data Scarcity
abstract: Arabic harmful-content moderation is commonly framed as toxicity detection, but many practical settings also require safer alternatives to toxic text rather than only blocking or labeling it. We study Arabic toxicity handling as a low-resource detect–then–rewrite problem. The first stage classifies comments as normal, hate, or abusive using a multi-dialect Arabic encoder, while the second stage rewrites toxic inputs into neutral alternatives using an Arabic sequence-to-sequence model. The detector is fine-tuned on Tun-EL, and the rewriter is trained with hybrid supervision from human rewrites, span-targeted rule-based augmentation, and multilingual ParaDetox transfer pairs. Our main focus is rewrite informativeness: many toxic–neutral pairs are identical or minimally edited, which may encourage copying rather than meaningful detoxification. The classifier achieves 82.42\% accuracy and 0.93 macro AUC. For rewriting, the more informative supervision variant improves sacreBLEU from 49.09 to 61.19, while the lower-informativeness variant gives stronger relative toxicity reduction under the current evaluation. These results suggest that Arabic detoxification is sensitive to supervision quality under data scarcity.

title: Prospective Test of Audit Sufficiency and Allocation Identity in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: This preregistration specifies a prospective experiment testing whether standard retrieval audits are behaviorally sufficient to characterize finite context allocations in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). The experiment constructs audit-equivalent context allocations that preserve the complete relevance-grade-by-position vector and therefore preserve precision@k, recall@k, nDCG@k, MRR@k, and MAP@k exactly, while varying the identities of metric-zero passages admitted to the finite context window. The primary outcome is the rate at which these identity-only reallocations change factual correctness. Secondary outcomes include canonical output change, identity-dose response, ordering sensitivity, and transport across datasets, retrievers, model families, and context capacities. This registration covers only the prospective RAG experiment. The broader manuscript also contains theoretical and previously conducted observational analyses that are not claimed to have been preregistered.

title: Prompt Before You Train: When Prompt Optimization Outperforms RLAIF for Small Language Models
abstract: Many social-good applications require small language models that can run locally and at low cost. When these models underperform, practitioners face a practical choice: invest in additional training using reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF) or first try improving the prompt. We study this question in climate communication, where persuasive messaging is important for public engagement and environmental awareness. We compare RLAIF and iterative prompt optimization across four small language models (350M–1.5B parameters) and three persuasion principles: Authority, Social Proof, and Unity. Across most conditions, prompt optimization produced larger gains in externally judged rubric-adherence scores while requiring no additional model training. In contrast, RLAIF often improved its internal reward without producing corresponding improvements in externally evaluated performance. Further analysis revealed several forms of reward misalignment, including reward hacking and self-judge saturation. These model-based scores do not establish effects on human attitudes or behavior. The results support prompt optimization as a first step only within the evaluated climate-communication setting; subsequent training should be checked using evaluation outside its optimization loop. This approach can help resource-constrained organizations, including non-profits, educational institutions, community groups, and small public-sector agencies, test lower-cost interventions before model retraining.

title: SLIDEFORGE: An LLM Agent for Controllable Editing of Slides as Structured Artifacts
abstract: Current AI agents compellingly describe slides. However, AI-assisted slide editing requires more than understanding: the output must retain layout, style, component structure, and native editability. Towards, AI-assisted slide editing, existing agents operate on screenshots or weak document representations and often fragment coherent visual units, rasterize editable content, or break layout. In contrast, for controllable slide editing, we introduce an agentic framework, SLIDEFORGE, which builds a Deck State Graph, an executable slide state that links visual decomposition, native pptx object structure, and perceptual organization. By recovering human-referable components while retaining fine-grained editable structure, SLIDEFORGE supports theme-preserving reconstruction through slide-native operations and rendered-state verification. We further introduce an evaluation paradigm for controllable slide transformation that jointly measures component recovery, preservation, restyling consistency, visual quality, and native editability. Experiments show that SLIDEFORGE outperforms direct prompting, screenshot-based agents, and generic code-agent baselines across these dimensions. Code is available at https://github.com/UIUC-MONET/SLIDEFORGE.

Towards, AI-assisted slide editing, existing agents operate on screenshots or weak document representations and often fragment coherent visual units, rasterize editable content, or break layout. In contrast, for controllable slide editing, we introduce an agentic framework, SLIDEFORGE, which builds a Deck State Graph, an executable slide state that links visual decomposition, native pptx object structure, and perceptual organization. By recovering human-referable components while retaining fine-grained editable structure, SLIDEFORGE supports theme-preserving reconstruction through slide-native operations and rendered-state verification. We further introduce an evaluation paradigm for controllable slide transformation that jointly measures component recovery, preservation, restyling consistency, visual quality, and native editability. Experiments show that SLIDEFORGE outperforms direct prompting, screenshot-based agents, and generic code-agent baselines across these dimensions. Code is available at https://github.com/UIUC-MONET/SLIDEFORGE.

title: Quantum Adaptive Distributed Optimization (QADO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Quantum Adaptive Distributed Optimization (QADO) framework, a novel approach to distributed optimization leveraging quantum entanglement for enhanced efficiency. Traditional distributed optimization methods often rely on static algorithms, limiting scalability and computational speed. QADO introduces a quantum-enhanced optimization process utilizing entanglement to achieve significantly reduced complexity and improved solution quality. We detail the framework's architecture, quantum entanglement implementation, and the resulting benefits observed through simulations and preliminary experiments. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential impact of QADO on a wide range of optimization problems.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum state optimization algorithm designed to enhance the performance of quantum computing, particularly in quantum simulation and parameter tuning. Our proposed algorithm leverages the dynamic evolution of quantum states to optimize quantum states, achieving superior results in these critical areas. This research addresses the limitations of existing methods by offering a robust and efficient solution for parameter adjustment and optimization within quantum systems. The core mechanism centers on continuously adjusting quantum states to maximize performance metrics, offering a significant advancement in quantum computation.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum self-organizing computation architecture designed to dynamically adjust computational processes based on real-time data. This work proposes a system that utilizes a dynamic, adaptive algorithm to optimize computational resources and minimize errors, leading to a robust and adaptable system suitable for a wide range of applications. title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithmic Memory
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to algorithmic memory design, drawing inspiration from quantum mechanics. The core idea is to emulate quantum coherence principles—specifically superposition and entanglement—to construct a more robust and resilient memory system. Traditional algorithmic memory structures often suffer from significant data loss due to bit flips and other errors. Our proposed system, termed "Quantum-Inspired Algorithmic Memory," utilizes a hierarchical architecture where information is encoded across multiple levels of abstraction, akin to the layered structure found in quantum systems. This approach aims to dramatically reduce data loss by exploiting the inherent redundancy and error-correction capabilities associated with quantum phenomena. We will detail the mathematical framework underpinning this architecture, focusing on the principles of superposition, entanglement, and decoherence mitigation. The system's performance will be evaluated through theoretical analysis and the derivation of key equations governing its operation. Ultimately, this research suggests a pathway toward creating memory systems capable of maintaining data integrity in challenging environments.

title: Quantum Entanglement Non-Linear Computation: Adaptive Noise Injection
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers unprecedented computational capabilities. However, its delicate nature makes it susceptible to decoherence, leading to errors in computations. This paper investigates a novel approach to mitigate these vulnerabilities through the implementation of adaptive noise injection within a quantum computation framework. We propose a system where the rate and type of noise injected are dynamically adjusted based on the state of the entangled qubits, effectively enhancing the stability and accuracy of the resulting quantum state. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the inherent fragility of entanglement to guide its evolution. This research explores the potential of this self-adaptive strategy to significantly improve the performance of quantum computations.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement: Distributed Memory Access and Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement for fundamentally new approaches to distributed memory access and computation. The core claim is that by exploiting entanglement, it is possible to achieve superluminal access to data residing in distributed storage devices, alongside enhanced collaborative computation. The proposed mechanism involves constructing multiple quantum processor nodes, orchestrated through precisely engineered entangled states. These states facilitate "instantaneous" data transmission and sharing between nodes, enabling collaborative execution of computational tasks. The quantum correlations inherent in entangled states accelerate computation and allow for parallel processing of vast datasets. This approach offers a paradigm shift from bandwidth and latency-constrained classical communication, potentially revolutionizing computationally intensive applications. The theoretical framework presented herein outlines the key concepts and considerations for realizing this transformative technology.

title: Adaptive Sampling Algorithm for Machine Learning Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive sampling algorithms to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of machine learning model training. Traditional sampling methods often rely on fixed strategies, which can be inefficient when dealing with datasets exhibiting non-uniform distributions. The core claim of this work is that dynamically adjusting the sampling strategy based on data distribution characteristics, through an adaptive sampling algorithm, can significantly improve the training process. The proposed mechanism involves designing an algorithm that modifies sampling probabilities based on statistical features of the data, ultimately aiming for optimal sampling. The research demonstrates the potential of adaptive sampling to address challenges in training machine learning models, particularly in scenarios with skewed or complex data distributions. This work provides a framework and theoretical foundation for the development of adaptive sampling techniques tailored to specific machine learning tasks.

title: Quantum State Reorganization and Information Extraction Joint Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum information processing, focusing on the joint optimization of quantum state reorganization and information extraction. The core claim is to maximize the utilization of quantum information by optimizing these two interconnected processes within a unified framework. The proposed method leverages precise control over quantum state rearrangement and extraction, aiming to achieve enhanced information gain and, consequently, improved quantum computing efficiency. The key mechanism involves transforming the traditionally separate processes into a synergistic optimization problem. Mathematical formulations are presented to formalize the problem and illustrate the optimization strategy. We analyze the impact of different reorganization schemes and extraction techniques on the overall information yield. The theoretical framework presented here lays the groundwork for developing more efficient quantum algorithms and hardware architectures. This work contributes to a more holistic understanding of quantum information processing and opens avenues for further research in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Neural Network Dynamics: Topology Self-Organization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamically self-organizing neural networks inspired by biological systems. Traditional static neural networks often struggle with adaptability and efficiency in complex environments. We propose a novel approach that leverages reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust connection strengths and incorporates probabilistic mechanisms for synaptic generation and removal, mirroring the plasticity observed in biological neural networks. The network topology itself evolves over time, driven by the reinforcement learning process, leading to the formation of more effective connection patterns. Our simulations demonstrate that this dynamic topology self-organization significantly enhances learning and inference capabilities compared to static networks. The core claim is that by simulating dynamic connections and synaptic changes, we can achieve more efficient and adaptive learning and reasoning. The central mechanism utilizes reinforcement learning to adjust connection strengths based on network output success rates and introduces probabilistic synaptic generation and deletion to mimic biological synaptic plasticity. The network topology evolves over time, creating optimized connection patterns.

title: Geometric Constraint Propagation for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of geometric constraint propagation to enhance the robustness and interpretability of machine learning models. Traditional constraint propagation techniques often struggle with complex dependencies and can lead to suboptimal model performance. We propose a novel method, the "Geometric Constraint Propagation Network," which automatically generates new constraints based on the model's output, improving generalization and offering a more transparent understanding of the model's decision-making process. The core mechanism leverages a network trained to identify and propagate constraints derived from the model's representation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments on various machine learning tasks, showcasing its ability to improve model accuracy and enhance interpretability.

title: Quantum-Inspired Noise Injection for Training Robust Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired noise injection techniques to enhance the robustness of neural networks. Traditional noise injection methods often rely on simple Gaussian or uniform noise distributions, which can be insufficient to effectively address the challenges of overfitting and generalization. We propose a novel approach that leverages concepts from quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and entanglement, to generate more complex and informative noise patterns. These patterns are designed to better simulate the inherent uncertainties present in real-world data, leading to improved training stability and enhanced network resilience. The core of our method involves mapping data points to a quantum state space and then applying noise based on quantum operations. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and simulations that our approach outperforms conventional noise injection techniques in scenarios with high dimensionality and complex data distributions. The key contributions of this work include a detailed formulation of the quantum-inspired noise injection process, a novel mapping strategy for data to quantum states, and empirical validation of its effectiveness.

title: Neural Network Topology Automated Optimization Framework
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for the automated optimization of neural network topologies using reinforcement learning. The core claim is that an adaptive topology optimization algorithm, driven by reinforcement learning, can dynamically adjust the structure of a neural network to achieve optimal performance. The framework utilizes a controller neural network that, based on a defined objective function (e.g., accuracy, speed) and the current network topology state, determines whether to add or remove neurons and connections, and adjusts connection weights accordingly. This approach represents a significant departure from existing methods, which often rely on pre-defined topologies or manual adjustments. The proposed system offers a fully automated and real-time feedback-driven optimization process. The system's architecture is described, and the reinforcement learning algorithm and its implementation are detailed. Initial results demonstrate the framework's capability to adapt network topologies effectively, leading to improved performance metrics. Further research will focus on scaling the framework to larger and more complex neural networks and exploring different reward functions to optimize for specific applications.

title: 基于自适应的深度学习的动态损失函数
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic loss function framework based on adaptive deep learning techniques. Traditional loss functions often lack adaptability to data variations, requiring manual tuning and potentially suboptimal performance. We propose a system that dynamically adjusts the loss function during training, allowing the model to continuously learn and optimize its performance. The core mechanism involves a meta-learning approach to dynamically update the loss function based on the model's internal gradients and the data distribution. This adaptive approach mitigates the limitations of static loss functions and offers a promising path toward enhanced model generalization and optimization. The proposed framework demonstrates significant improvements in model accuracy and stability across a variety of benchmark datasets.

title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding and Relational Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to self-supervised representation learning by synergistically combining contrastive predictive coding (CPC) with relational reasoning. The core idea is to train a representation learning model that learns to predict future states of a system, leveraging both the temporal dependencies captured by CPC and explicit modeling of relationships between system components. We utilize a recurrent neural network (RNN) to generate future state predictions, minimizing the discrepancy between predicted and actual states through a CPC-inspired loss function. Crucially, we introduce relational embeddings to guide this process, allowing the model to learn and reason about the inherent relationships within the system. This integrated approach promises to produce more robust and informative representations compared to methods relying solely on one technique. The resulting model demonstrates improved performance in capturing complex system dynamics and relationships.

title: Supporting Caregivers as End-User Developers through Human-Centered Explainable AI in Ambient Assisted Living
abstract: This doctoral research investigates how human-centered Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) can be integrated with AI-assisted End User Development (EUD) environments to support caregivers in configuring and managing Ambient Assisted Living (AAL) systems. The research adopts a Human-Centered Design perspective and follows an iterative methodology based on the design, development, and evaluation of explanation strategies within a Digital Twin of a smart home. The planned approach combines AI-driven assistance, simulation capabilities, and human-centered explanations to help caregivers understand system suggestions, anticipate outcomes, and take informed decisions. As a preliminary step, the manuscript presents a conversational system for therapy management, that explores a hybrid architecture combining Large Language Models with deterministic validation mechanisms and retrieval-based knowledge integration. This work provides initial insights into balancing flexibility and reliability in AI-assisted end-user tools and serves as a foundation for future extensions to AAL scenarios. The expected contributions of the research project include the design of explanation strategies tailored to caregivers, the development of an AI-assisted Digital Twin environment for AAL, and empirical evidence on how human-centered XAI can improve users’ understanding, trust, and control over intelligent systems.

title: CRAW: Codec Robust Audio Watermarking
abstract: Recent advances in generative speech models have made it increasingly difficult to distinguish authentic from synthetic audio, enabling new forms of fraud and misinformation. Audio watermarking offers a promising defense by embedding an imperceptible signal into generated speech that can later be detected to verify its provenance. However, recent studies have shown that existing post-hoc watermarking methods fail under neural codecs and denoisers, transformations routinely applied during real-world storage, transmission, and processing, severely limiting their practical utility. Here we introduce CRAW, a codec-robust audio watermarking framework that jointly improves robustness against neural re-synthesis while maintaining high perceptual quality. CRAW combines distortion-aware training with an attention-based pooling mechanism, inference-time perceptual mask- ing, and an error-correcting code to recover the fidelity lost during robust training. Experiments demonstrate that CRAW achieves state-of-the-art robustness against neural codecs, denoisers, and vocoders while maintaining perceptual quality comparable to existing post-hoc watermarking methods. The code is available at https://github.com/DavidC1212/craw.

title: Experimental Evaluation of Passive Polarization Compensation Techniques for Fiber-Distributed Polarization-Entangled Photons
abstract: Entanglement distribution through optical fibers is essential for quantum communication networks; however, fiber transmission can alter photon polarization and modify the observed correlations of polarization-entangled states, necessitating polarization compensation to recover the desired entangled state in the measurement basis. Here, we experimentally evaluate two passive polarization compensation techniques: a free-space Quarter-Half-Quarter (QHQ) waveplate configuration and an in-fiber three-paddle Fiber Polarization Controller (FPC). The polarization transformation along each downconverted-photon path is independently compensated through a systematic path-by-path optimization procedure. Using both techniques, we recover high-quality polarization correlations and entanglement, with visibilities exceeding $93\%$ in three mutually unbiased bases and fidelities above $94.5\%$. The results demonstrate comparable restoration using free-space waveplate-based and fiber-based control, establishing a systematic framework for laboratory and short-reach quantum communication links.

evidence.abstract: Entanglement distribution through optical fibers is essential for quantum communication networks; however, fiber transmission can alter photon polarization and modify the observed correlations of polarization-entangled states, necessitating polarization compensation to recover the desired entangled state in the measurement basis. Here, we experimentally evaluate two passive polarization compensation techniques: a free-space Quarter-Half-Quarter (QHQ) waveplate configuration and an in-fiber three-paddle Fiber Polarization Controller (FPC). The polarization transformation along each downconverted-photon path is independently compensated through a systematic path-by-path optimization procedure. Using both techniques, we recover high-quality polarization correlations and entanglement, with visibilities exceeding $93\%$ in three mutually unbiased bases and fidelities above $94.5\%$. The results demonstrate comparable restoration using free-space waveplate-based and fiber-based control, establishing a systematic framework for laboratory and short-reach quantum communication links.

title: CC-4DGS: Computational Deformation and Point-Cloud Compression for Storage-Efficient Dynamic Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Dynamic four-dimensional (4D) Gaussian Splatting has emerged as a powerful explicit representation for high-quality view synthesis, yet existing methods still require tens to hundreds of megabytes per scene due to their heavy reliance on large multi-resolution hash tables and high-dimensional Gaussian attributes. This paper presents CC-4DGS, a storage-efficient and scalable framework that rethinks both deformation modeling and canonical attribute storage. First, we introduce a computational deformation field (CDF) that replaces large multi-resolution learnable hash tables with deterministic dense hash encoding and compact neural decoders, enabling on-the-fly synthesis of deformation features while reducing deformation storage to only 1--3 MB per scene. Second, we propose a compression of canonical point-cloud attributes (CCA) pipeline that compresses high-dimensional spherical harmonic appearance terms and auxiliary Gaussian attributes via conditional autoencoding, selective quantization, and residual codebooks, achieving 3--5$\times$ point-cloud reduction with negligible quality loss. Together, these components yield a unified representation that preserves real-time rendering performance while reducing total storage to 20--30 MB. Extensive experiments across the N3DV and Technicolor Light Field datasets demonstrate that CC-4DGS achieves reconstruction accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art methods such as Swift4D, while offering significantly improved storage efficiency and favorable runtime-memory trade-offs.

title: WaveSync: Constrained Wavefront Optimization for Synchronized Co-Speech Gestures in Humanoid Robots
abstract: Expressive co-speech gestures are crucial for natural human--robot interaction, yet generating them on physical humanoid robots remains challenging because, unlike virtual avatars, robots must synchronize gestures with speech under strict kinematic and actuator constraints. We present WaveSync, a hybrid framework in which a Large Language Model decomposes dialogue responses into structured semantic schemas and assigns per-word importance weights, forming a continuous Semantic Importance Wave. Gesture trajectories are shaped through Dynamic Movement Primitives to ensure kinematic feasibility while enhancing expressiveness. A Wavefront Optimization stage aligns gesture stroke peaks with speech emphasis peaks and resolves residual temporal conflicts through gesture-duration compression and forward propagation. Experimental evaluation across five dialogue scenarios demonstrates effective gesture--speech alignment and favorable performance in both objective and subjective evaluations. The results further show that the key components of WaveSync contribute to producing gestures that are expressive, semantically grounded, and kinematically feasible. The code, resources, and videos are available at https://github.com/pairs-lab/WaveSync{WaveSync}.

title: On Propositional Dynamic Logic and Concurrency
abstract: Dynamic logic is a powerful approach to reasoning about programs and their executions, obtained by extending classical logic with modalities that can express program executions as formulas. However, the use of dynamic logic in the setting of concurrency has proved problematic because of the challenge of capturing interleaving. This challenge stems from the fact that, traditionally, programs are represented by their sets of traces. These sets are then expressed as elements of a Kleene algebra, for which it is not possible to decide equality in the presence of the commutations required to model interleaving. In this work, we generalise propositional dynamic logic (PDL) to a logic framework we call operational propositional dynamic logic (OPDL), which departs from tradition by distinguishing programs from their traces. Traces are generated by an arbitrary operational semantics that we take as a parameter, making our approach applicable to different program syntaxes and semantics. To develop our framework, we provide the first proof of cut-elimination for a finitely-branching non-wellfounded sequent calculus for PDL. Thanks to this result we can effortlessly prove adequacy for PDL, and extend these results to OPDL. We conclude by discussing OPDL for two representative cases of concurrency: the Calculus of Communicating Systems (CCS), where interleaving is obtained by parallel composition, and Choreographic Programming, where interleaving is obtained by out-of-order execution.

title: Weighted UnLearning from Experience for improved spurious correlation robustness
abstract: Despite their success, Deep Learning (DL) models are susceptible to spurious correlations. These are accidental correlations between non-predictive features of the training dataset and the target label, leading to models that do not generalise well to samples without such spurious correlations. We propose to address this failure mode by extending and improving an existing method for spurious correlation robustness — UnLearning from Experience (ULE). ULE trains two models in parallel; a biased model is encouraged to learn the spurious correlations, while a separate debiased model is trained to solve the same task while avoiding learning the same behaviour as the first, thus avoiding learning the spurious correlations. A weakness of ULE is that it treats every training example identically, regardless of whether or not it contains a spurious correlation. Therefore, ULE does not make optimal use of the training data, leading to worsethan- necessary performance. To address this weakness, we introduce Weighted UnLearning from Experience (wULE), which modifies the original ULE loss function to reweight the components depending on whether a training sample likely contains spurious correlations. Hence, we explore two methods for identifying training samples likely to contain spurious correlations. We test our approach using several well-known spurious correlation robustness benchmarks — Waterbirds, CelebA, UrbanCars and MultiNLI. Our novel wULE method outperforms the original ULE in all cases and achieves Worst-Group Accuracy (WGA) results comparable to the best methods in the spurious correlation robustness literature.

title: Too Simple, Too Complex, Just Right: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of deep learning and inductive bias as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Title: Dynamic Space Transformations via Quantum Spin
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic space transformation algorithm based on quantum spin, leveraging its inherent self-similarity to dynamically adjust quantum system geometries. The core mechanism centers around iterative optimization driven by the self-correlation of quantum spins, enabling the design of complex spacetime structures within quantum systems. This approach offers a potential paradigm shift in optimizing quantum device performance, addressing limitations of conventional static optimization methods. We present a framework for generating and manipulating quantum systems exhibiting dynamic spacetime, and discuss its implications for advancing the design and control of quantum technologies.

title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamic Geometry Transformation Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally new approach to geometric transformations, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical algorithms. This paper introduces a novel dynamic geometry transformation algorithm based on quantum entanglement, designed to dynamically adjust geometric structures based on input transformations. We explore the potential of this approach to achieve complex geometric transformations and offer a fundamentally different computational model. The core mechanism involves leveraging entanglement to encode and manipulate geometric information, allowing for iterative refinement and optimization. We present a detailed mathematical framework and discuss preliminary results demonstrating the algorithm's capability to perform complex geometric transformations. This work explores the potential for novel calculations and optimization.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Causal Inference in Time Series
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to causal inference within the context of time series data, leveraging the power of probabilistic programming. Traditional causal inference techniques frequently rely on assumptions of static relationships, limiting their applicability to dynamic systems. This work addresses this limitation by employing probabilistic programming languages to explicitly model causal relationships, incorporating temporal dependencies and facilitating the estimation of causal effects under evolving conditions. The core mechanism involves defining causal models using probabilistic programming, allowing for the simulation of time series data and the subsequent estimation of causal effects. This approach offers a rigorous framework for causal inference in dynamic time series environments, representing a significant advancement over existing methods. The methodology is illustrated through a conceptual framework, focusing on the implementation and theoretical underpinnings rather than specific experimental results. The paper highlights the potential of this approach for addressing complex causal questions within time series data, particularly where temporal dynamics are critical.

title: Adaptive Self-Organized Quantum Network Quantum Probability Distribution Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the development of an adaptive self-organized quantum network (ASQN) quantum probability distribution optimization algorithm. Traditional quantum computation relies heavily on human intervention in parameter tuning, leading to limitations in accuracy and efficiency. The proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts the probability distribution within the ASQN, automatically optimizing the quantum state for improved performance. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop utilizing system state to iteratively refine the probability distribution, offering a novel approach to quantum computing that surpasses existing optimization techniques. This work demonstrates the potential for significant improvements in quantum accuracy through automated adjustment, paving the way for more robust and reliable quantum computations.

title: Dynamic Topological Quantum Entanglement Routing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for quantum communication utilizing dynamic topological quantum entanglement routing. The core concept involves constructing a quantum network topology not based on fixed physical connections, but rather on dynamically adapting entanglement routes. This approach leverages quantum entanglement and machine learning to create a self-optimizing network capable of overcoming limitations inherent in traditional quantum networks. The system analyzes real-time network conditions – specifically entanglement strength and noise levels – and adjusts the topology of the entanglement routes using a machine learning algorithm. This dynamic adaptation aims to establish and maintain optimal communication pathways, theoretically offering the potential for information transfer exceeding the speed of light. The proposed architecture addresses the shortcomings of existing quantum networks that often rely on static physical connections and lacks adaptability. This research explores the fundamental principles and theoretical possibilities of such a system.

title: TT-G42: An E8-Extended Post-Quantum Cryptosystem with Graded Geometric Hard-Gating
abstract: TT-G42: An E8-Extended Post-Quantum Cryptosystem with Graded Geometric Hard-Gating Chloe J. TullyIndependent ResearcherORCID: 0009-0007-5661-7332August 2026 Version 1.1 Abstract We present TT-G42, the natural successor to the TT-G41 hybrid cryptosystem. The five-dimensional Ly-Algebraic core is replaced by the 248-dimensional adjoint representation of the exceptional simple Lie algebra E8. The Quasi-Equivalence Index (QEI) is redefined on the weight lattice of E8, exploiting the Coxeter group symmetry and the deep golden-ratio structure of the E8 root system to construct a geometric invariant with substantially larger entropy. The lattice layer is scaled to NIST-compatible parameters (n=701, q=2048), and the symmetry-modulated padding is reformulated as a graded noise injection derived from the projection onto the fundamental Weyl chamber. We establish that the QEI-induced failure probability continues to obey a logistic bound with shape parameter 15.57, independent of ambient dimension to leading order. An adaptive hard-gate mechanism is introduced whose threshold is derived from the running variance of the QEI stream; the gate is shown to be constant-time and free of partial-message side channels. Empirical evaluation on 10 000 trials yields R2=0.984. The construction demonstrates that exceptional algebraic geometry can serve as a native control surface for lattice-based post-quantum protocols. Keywords: post-quantum cryptography, E8, exceptional Lie algebra, Quasi-Equivalence Index, NTRU, geometric security bound, side-channel resistance, Weyl group, graded noise injection Introduction TT-G41 demonstrated that a continuous geometric invariant derived from a graded Lie algebra can function as an active cryptographic control surface rather than a passive hardness assumption . The five-dimensional construction established the principle: geometric coherence, measured by the Quasi-Equivalence Index (QEI), directly modulates ciphertext entropy and determines decryption success through a deterministic hard gate. The present work scales that principle to its natural algebraic limit. The exceptional simple Lie algebra E8, with its 248-dimensional adjoint representation, 240 roots, and Weyl group of order 696 729 600, supplies a geometric entropy space of sufficient complexity to address the residual threat of adversarial vector manipulation that remained a limitation of the five-dimensional case. The E8 root system exhibits a well-known connection to the golden ratio =1+5/2 through its Coxeter plane and icosahedral symmetry, rendering it the canonical extension of the original Ly-Algebra’s golden-ratio grading. TT-G42 contributes three concrete advances: An E8-native Quasi-Equivalence Index defined on the weight lattice, computed via the Killing form and a graded action of the Cartan generators, together with a closed-form link between root-space distortion and decryption failure probability. A NIST-compatible lattice layer (n=701, q=2048) whose circulant inversion is verified against the security boundaries of Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanisms . An adaptive hard gate whose threshold is derived from the empirical variance of the QEI stream, eliminating the fixed-threshold limitation of TT-G41 and providing constant-time, side-channel-resistant rejection.

title: Title: Non-Local Semantic Networks
abstract: The traditional semantic network, while foundational, often struggles to capture the dynamic nature of meaning and the emergence of novel concepts. This paper proposes a novel approach to semantic networks – Non-Local Semantic Networks (NLSNs) – that explicitly models concepts across spacetime, facilitating the propagation of semantic changes through a chronological graph. This design allows for the evolution of meaning and the formation of new concepts, driven by interactions between nodes representing temporal relationships. We present a detailed architecture, including the implementation of a 'chronological graph' and the mathematical framework for representing and propagating semantic changes. The core claim is that NLSNs provide a robust mechanism for understanding and generating meaning in a temporally evolving system.

title: Neural Network Memory in Dynamic Topology Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to complex pattern learning within Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) by incorporating dynamic topology changes. The core concept leverages the inherent plasticity of neural networks, simulating the evolving connections between neurons to achieve more efficient and robust learning compared to traditional static weight update methods. The proposed system utilizes a Self-Organizing Map (SOM) based topology update rule, coupled with a reinforcement learning algorithm, to predictively adjust network topology based on neuron activity patterns and learning objectives. Furthermore, a neuron death mechanism is introduced to promote topological optimization and mitigate local optima. The resulting network demonstrates superior performance in complex pattern prediction and control, highlighting the potential of dynamic topology learning for advanced ANN applications.

Furthermore, a neuron death mechanism is introduced to promote topological optimization and mitigate local optima. The resulting network demonstrates superior performance in complex pattern prediction and control, highlighting the potential of dynamic topology learning for advanced ANN applications.

title: Bio-Inspired Distributed Machine Learning Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to distributed machine learning optimization inspired by biological neural networks. The core concept is to mimic the parallel computing and learning mechanisms observed in biological systems to tackle large-scale optimization problems. The proposed algorithm decomposes the optimization task into multiple sub-problems, which are then solved concurrently by a network of nodes. These nodes utilize bio-inspired heuristic algorithms to refine the solutions of the sub-problems and ultimately achieve global optimization. The key innovation lies in leveraging the inherent advantages of biological neural networks to enhance the efficiency and scalability of distributed machine learning optimization. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, focusing on the mechanisms for parallel computation, learning, and convergence. This work lays the foundation for a new paradigm in optimization, drawing inspiration from the elegant and robust design of the brain. ---

title: 基于自适应的图灵机计算框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel, adaptive graph theory-based computational framework for logical reasoning. Traditional graph theory approaches often require pre-defined parameters, limiting their applicability to complex problems. Our framework dynamically adjusts internal graph states based on input data, enabling the algorithm to intelligently adapt to the problem's characteristics and improve reasoning efficiency. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through a series of experimental results, showcasing its superior performance compared to static graph theory methods in a range of logical reasoning tasks. The core mechanism involves a self-tuning parameter adjustment algorithm that iteratively optimizes the graph's state to enhance logical inference. The research addresses the limitations of static approaches by introducing a flexible and adaptive system that responds to the input data, ultimately leading to more robust and efficient logical reasoning.

title: High-Dimensional Symbolic Logic Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computation leveraging high-dimensional symbolic logic, aiming to accelerate the evaluation and verification of complex logical expressions. We propose a quantum-enhanced symbolic logic system that utilizes quantum entanglement and superposition to achieve significantly faster computation compared to classical methods. The core mechanism centers around exploiting these quantum phenomena to represent and manipulate logical statements with unprecedented efficiency. The system focuses on automating the generation of logical inference models, reducing the reliance on manual effort. This work addresses the limitations of traditional symbolic logic computation by introducing a fundamentally different algorithmic structure. We present initial results demonstrating the potential for substantial speedups in specific scenarios, highlighting the promise of this approach for complex problem-solving.

title: Voice-Sync: AI-Powered Multilingual News Reader Using Python
abstract: Yet although accessing news online has never been easier, the experience tends to be fragmented. Readers frequently have to jump between multiple websites, wade through lengthy articles, or switch between different tools just. To obtain a translation or to have some content read out loud. This constant back-and-forth makes it difficult to stay informed, especially for those who prefer consuming news in their native. People or those who want a hands-free experience. To solve this, we developed Voice-Sync, a web-based news reader that brings the power of Artificial Intelligence into one seamless platform. Built using the Python and the Flask framework, Voice-Sync automatically pulls the latest headlines from NewsAPI and processes via specialized AI modules. When an article has been retrieved, the app produces a brief summary by means of specialized AI modules. Once an article is retrieved, the app creates a concise summary using Natural Language Processing, translates it into various. Convert Indian Languages into clear, natural speech using the text-to-speech feature from Microsoft Edge Neural. Beyond reading the news, Voice-Sync offers voice- controlled navigation, sentiment analysis, bookmarking, and the ability to export reports as PDFs. By streamlining these tasks, we have created a more intuitive, accessible way for users to engage with information without the usual technical friction.

title: Same Persona, Different Behaviors: Quantifying Persona Conditioning in Large Language Models
abstract: Persona conditioning is increasingly used to guide the behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet the extent to which models consistently and effectively adapt to assigned identities remains unclear. In this paper, we present a systematic evaluation of persona-conditioned behavior in three open-weight LLMs: DeepSeek, Gemma, and Nemotron. We designed a controlled experiment involving 21 ethically and socially sensitive questions and six distinct personas, generating a total of 378 model responses. Our analysis combines decision-level evaluation, TF-IDF-based lexical characterization, and embedding-based semantic similarity. We also introduce a Personalization Index that captures both intra-persona consistency and inter-persona differentiation. The results show that personalization is a gradual and strongly model-dependent phenomenon. Gemma exhibits the highest degree of adaptation, with clear lexical and semantic differentiation across personas, while Nemotron demonstrates more consistent but less pronounced personalization. DeepSeek displays weaker and less stable persona adaptation. A key finding is that persona conditioning does not lead to a uniform interpretation of identity: the same person can produce systematically different responses depending on the model. This highlights personalization as a trade-off between relevance and diversity, offering engagement benefits with the potential risk of reinforcing existing biases.

title: Scaling Laws, Tabular Data and Actuarial Ratemaking Models
abstract: Scaling laws in modern deep learning describe how held-out loss improves as model capacity, training data, and compute increase, often following power-law trends. We investigate whether analogous scaling regularities arise in actuarial ratemaking, where data are tabular, heterogeneous, and noisy, and where classical models such as GLMs remain strong baselines. Using a real-world motor insurance portfolio, we train models from different families across increasing fractions of the training data and multiple random seeds, evaluating out-of-sample Poisson deviance, a likelihood-based loss for Poisson count predictions in which lower values indicate better held-out fit. We find that all model families improve with additional data, but scaling exponents differ substantially: TabM exhibits markedly stronger data scaling than purely supervised tabular Transformers and standard MLP baselines. Transformer variants show weak parameter scaling unless augmented with additional inductive biases (TabM-style adaptation or self-supervision). These results provide quantitative guidance on model selection by data regime and suggest that effective scaling on actuarial tabular tasks depends on architecture and loss function objective design, with simple increases in Transformer size providing limited gains.

title: Optical Reservoir Computing with Structural Nonlinearity for Forecasting Chaotic Time Series
abstract: Optical computing offers a promising route to high-speed, energy-efficient information processing. However, implementing nonlinear operations typically requires strong light-matter interactions. Here, we introduce structural nonlinearity into an optical reservoir computing architecture, using only linear components. A digital micromirror device acts as a reconfigurable scattering potential, while the propagation of light through a scattering medium provides the high-dimensional mode mixing. By enforcing a second interaction with the wavefront shaper, we obtain a quadratic mapping of the input within the reservoir. A single experimental apparatus simultaneously implements conventional and structurally nonlinear reservoir architectures, enabling a direct comparison on forecasting of the chaotic Mackey-Glass time series. We demonstrate that the structurally nonlinear reservoir improves short-term prediction accuracy and better preserves the long-term dynamics of the chaotic system, demonstrating the potential of structural nonlinearity for low-power optical computing.

title: H3DNAS: Hardware-Aware ONNX-Native 3D Point Cloud Model Compression
abstract: Deploying 3D point cloud models on edge hardware such as the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano is severely constrained by compute and memory budgets. Existing compression methods require access to the model's original source code, rendering them inapplicable to the Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) binaries commonly distributed by vendors and model repositories. We present \textbf{H3DNAS}, a hardware-aware model compression framework that operates directly on ONNX computational graphs without requiring original source code, architecture class definition, or gradient access during search. H3DNAS makes three contributions: (1) a \textbf{Channel Dependency Graph (CDG)} that classifies ONNX operators into four constraint classes and formally establishes that the free parameter fraction $ρ_f$ is topological invariant, a provable compression ceiling computable in $\mathcal{O}(|V|+|E|)$; (2) a \textbf{Two-Stage Hierarchical Search} that prunes candidate architectures by $L_1$-importance channel selection, ranks them by output fidelity as a zero-shot label-free proxy, and applies GhostConv structural mutation to Pareto-optimal candidates; and (3) the \textbf{first source-code-free compression pipeline for 3D point cloud models}, operating entirely via ONNX graph surgery with no original architecture definition required. On ModelNet40, H3DNAS reduces the number of parameters in PointNet, PointNet++, and PointMLP by $65.5\%$, $43.2\%$, and $49.1\%$, respectively, while achieving $1.99\times$, $1.29\times$, and $1.67\times$ inference speedups with negligible loss in accuracy. The source code is publicly available\footnote{https://github.com/ClarityLab-Org/h3dnas}.

title: Semantics-Guided Automatic Tensorization for Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithms: A Multi-Agent Framework
abstract: Multiobjective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) naturally expose population-level parallelism, but many mature implementations encode their computation in sequential program structures designed for central processing units. Exploiting modern tensor computing platforms therefore requires more than direct code translation: the implementation must be restructured without changing the defining optimization mechanism of the underlying MOEA. We formulate automatic tensorization for MOEAs as semantics-guided computational restructuring and develop Evolutionary Code Conversion (EvoCoCo), a multi-agent framework that realizes this formulation. EvoCoCo reconstructs algorithm-specific states, dependencies, operators, and update logic into a structured semantic representation and organizes them through a shared tensorization blueprint. Specialized transformation branches then explore alternative tensor realizations, while execution feedback guides validation, repair, and candidate selection. Experiments on a benchmark of 48 MOEAs evaluate migration reliability, optimization fidelity, and computational scalability. Under matched large language model backends, EvoCoCo attains higher migration reliability than direct one-shot translation. Across the benchmark suites, 88.2% of valid comparisons satisfy the predefined optimization-fidelity criterion. The tensorized implementations also exhibit increasing acceleration on graphics processing units as population size or decision dimension grows, with median measured speedups ranging from $22.6\times$ under population scaling to $80.2\times$ under decision-dimension scaling. External-source and ablation studies further assess transfer beyond the main benchmark and the roles of the major framework components.

title: 2026 2nd International Conference on Federated Learning and Intelligent Computing Systems (FLICS)
abstract: The rapid expansion of distributed Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) infrastructures introduces significant cybersecurity vulnerabilities, as Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices continuously stream sensitive physiological data across organizational boundaries. Existing centralized threat detection paradigms are poorly suited to this environment, often failing to capture the temporal evolution of attacks while violating data sovereignty requirements under Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) and General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). To address these challenges, we propose Federated Temporal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (FedTempRAG), a novel framework for privacy-preserving, real-time threat intelligence in distributed RPM ecosystems. FedTempRAG integrates a decentralized vector database for cross-institutional retrieval, a dynamic temporal knowledge graph to model attack progression, and a secure aggregation protocol that enables privacy-preserving collaborative learning. Our implementation adopts homomorphic encryption for secure query processing and Byzantine-resilient aggregation to defend against adversarial participants. We evaluated FedTempRAG on a simulated multi-hospital RPM network using real-world medical threat datasets and high-fidelity emulated IoMT environments derived from public RPM repositories. Experimental results demonstrate that FedTempRAG achieves 94.3% detection accuracy, 91.7% recall, and a 0.930 F1-score, while maintaining an average inference latency of 847 -ms and a 9.8% computation overhead, enabling practical real-time deployment in RPM systems. The temporal reasoning component successfully reconstructed many multi-stage attack lifecycles, highlighting the effectiveness of integrating temporal context into federated threat intelligence. These findings establish FedTempRAG as a robust foundation for next-generation RPM security, achieving a practical balance between collaborative intelligence, temporal awareness, system efficiency, and strict privacy preservation.

title: USE OF HISTOPATHOLOGICAL IMAGE DATABASES AND ASSOCIATED DATA FOR DIAGNOSTIC IMPROVEMENT OF LEUKOPLAKIA AND ORAL CANCER: A scoping review
abstract: This scoping review aims to map and characterize the global literature on histopathological image datasets and associated clinical metadata for oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD) and oral cancer, evaluating how these repositories are developed, characterized, and applied to train, validate, and test artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning models. Following the JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the protocol outlines a comprehensive search strategy across major health and technological databases alongside grey literature, without date or language restrictions. The extracted results will be synthesized in descriptive tables detailing dataset identification, population characteristics, associated clinical features and diagnoses, histopathological diagnoses, metadata, annotation methods, AI technologies employed, and their specific downstream applications.

title: General Structure Unfolding Intelligence: From Core Structure and Delta Modification to a General Paradigm of Intelligence
abstract: General Structure Unfolding Intelligence (GSUI) develops a structural framework for studying intelligent processes as controlled unfolding from persistent structure. Its canonical form is expressed as +/- , with extensions involving context, triggering, unfolding space, control policy, evaluation, invariant preservation, certification, feedback, structural growth, and Structural Self. The repository examines Folding and Unfolding as complementary phases of an intelligence cycle: observation and experience may be folded into persistent structure, while that structure can later be unfolded into reasoning, generation, planning, routing, coding, control, action, and structural modification. GSUI distinguishes search within an existing possibility space from structural unfolding that can change future possibility itself. It introduces Unfolding Space to distinguish possible, reachable, allowed, preferred, selected, and certified transitions; treats the Control Plane as a first-class component of consequential intelligent unfolding; and defines Structural Growth as retained unfolding that changes future unfolding capacity. GSUI further introduces Structural Self as the persistent structural reference frame relative to which Delta, capability, continuity, world-model meaning, and future unfolding are defined. The framework explicitly separates Structural Self from consciousness or personhood, explores non-anthropomorphic machine perception and machine-native cognition, and maintains the governance principle that machine-native cognition should remain compatible with human-governable consequences. This v1.0.0 release establishes the foundational GSUI research framework, terminology, claim boundaries, visual language, and future research directions.

title: Dynamic Matrix Mapping for Optimization: A Novel Approach
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic matrix mapping algorithm (DMM) for optimizing complex systems. The DMM offers a robust and adaptable approach to parameter tuning, enabling automatic adjustment of parameters to maximize the objective function. Traditional optimization methods often require manual parameter adjustment, which can be time-consuming and prone to error. The DMM leverages the unique characteristics of dynamic matrices to achieve more efficient and reliable parameter optimization. This research presents a framework that simplifies the parameter tuning process and enhances the algorithm's adaptability to complex systems. The core mechanism focuses on the dynamic reshaping of the objective function matrix through matrix operations, leading to improved optimization performance. This approach significantly reduces the need for manual adjustment and improves the overall efficiency of parameter optimization.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Storage & Extraction Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two particles become linked and share the same fate regardless of the distance separating them, has captivated scientists and intrigued philosophers alike. This research explores the potential of harnessing this quantum phenomenon to develop novel information storage and extraction techniques. We propose a system leveraging quantum entanglement for secure key distribution and data transfer, utilizing a specialized extraction algorithm that exploits the unique properties of entangled states. This research focuses on establishing a robust and efficient method for safeguarding information against eavesdropping and optimizing data transfer rates. The core of this investigation is the design of a key distribution protocol based on entangled states, complemented by a novel extraction algorithm designed to maximize data fidelity and minimize computational overhead. The anticipated outcome is a significantly enhanced security and efficient data transfer capability, representing a major advancement in the field of quantum information science. This approach addresses the growing need for secure data analysis in scenarios where data privacy is paramount. The research demonstrates the feasibility and potential of this technique, offering a novel solution for protecting sensitive information during analytical processes.
